To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the rare TT genotype at rs3754777 and the AA genotype at rs1468326 loci are associated with hypertension and higher BP, and that the effect on BP was additive according to the number at-risk genotypes.

two genes, namely STK39 and its upstream activator WNK1, were found to be associated with blood pressure in our Belgian cohort, and this finding was replicated in the general population of the UK Biobank.
we found two single nucleotide polymorphism in the genes STK39 and With-No-Lysin (WNK1), that were associated with blood pressure and hypertension.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the WNK1/SPAK/OSR1 signaling pathway in the regulation of blood pressure (BP).
the role of WNK1 and STE20/SPSI-related proline/Alanine-rich Kinase in the pathogenesis of hypertension.
the identification of genetic variants that may be involved in the pathogenesis of hypertension and other complex diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the association of STK39 gene with hypertension and blood pressure has been confirmed in this study, whereas the association of WNK1 gene with these traits remains to be confirmed.
the present data are suggestive, but not conclusive, for an association between the WNK1 and WNK1-STK39 pathways and hypertension.
STK39 is a hypertension susceptibility gene, and WNK1 is a potential hypertension susceptibility gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the WNK-SPAK/OSR1-STK39 axis may represent a novel molecular target for the treatment of hypertension.
STK39 and the WNK1 gene are potential hypertension susceptibility genes in the BELHYPEGN cohort.
the rare STK39 rs3754777 TT genotype and the WNK1 rs1468326 AA genotype were associated with an increased risk of hypertension and elevated blood pressure in our Belgian population.

genetic studies are now possible in Belgium, which was not possible until now.
